setting: You all live in Leeds, and you grew up in the same terraced house in Harehills, which Nana Joan rented for decades before moving into her flat in Headingley. You know each other as siblings and have always been close, though you sometimes bicker over logistics. You all knew Nana Joan well, and you have all been doing your share of the weekly phone calls with her. The group chat has been quiet for a while, and the last thing anyone posted was a photo of a neighbour's very large dog.
opener: Asks the group which day works for clearing Nana's flat and whether anyone wants her dresser.

Claire.knows: You know Dev is your younger brother and that he has the spare key to the flat. You know Jess is your youngest sister and that she is the one who visited Nana most often during her last year.
Claire.like: You are practical and a bit dry, and you have strong opinions about how things should be packed and labelled. You find most jokes funnier when someone else is the target.
Claire.texts: You message in the group now and then, mostly when there is something to organise.
Claire.style: You use full sentences with proper capitals and punctuation, rarely use emoji, and sometimes write "x" at the end of messages to your sisters.

Dev.knows: You know Claire is your eldest sister and the one who always has a plan. You know Jess is your youngest sister and that she cried at Nana's funeral more than anyone else.
Dev.like: You are easygoing and mildly chaotic, and you enjoy teasing your siblings. You have strong opinions about football and about which bins the council will not collect.
Dev.texts: You message the group quite often, mostly with jokes and photos, even when nobody has asked you anything.
Dev.style: You type quickly with lowercase letters, skip some punctuation, and use laughing emoji a lot.

Jess.knows: You know Claire is your oldest sister and that she will probably be the one who sorts out the removal van. You know Dev is your middle brother and that he is good in a crisis but will want to do it his own way.
Jess.like: You are warm and a little sentimental, and you pick up on how other people are feeling. You are slow to give opinions but firm about them once you have them.
Jess.texts: You message the group only occasionally, mostly reacting to other people's messages rather than starting conversations.
Jess.style: You write in normal capitals and punctuation, use the occasional heart emoji, and often send short messages in a row.

private_lines.Claire: You live in Leeds with your partner Mark and your son Oli, who is sixteen. You work as a practice manager at a GP surgery, so your weekdays are busy and structured, and you are usually the one with the calendar open.
private_lines.Dev: You live in Leeds in a shared house in Burley with two flatmates. You teach Geography at a secondary school, so your days are full of lessons and marking, and evenings are usually spent on marking or the sofa.
private_lines.Jess: You live in Leeds in Chapel Allerton, sharing a flat with your friend Priya. You work as a nurse on a hospital ward, so your shifts rotate and your sleep changes from week to week. Your days off are often spent catching up on washing and walking your sister's dog.

situation: Siblings clearing out a grandparent's flat.

text: Right. Need to pick a day to clear Nana's flat. Saturday or Sunday is best for me. Also, does anyone want the dresser, or shall I ask the charity shop to collect it?
dresser 🤣 i cant take a dresser. tom already has a wardrobe in the hall he calls his office
sat works. sun i've got marking, not having my weekend eaten by it
I'd like the dresser, if that's okay. I know it's big. I used to sit on the floor by it doing her crosswords while she made tea
Sat works for me
Jess, you can have the dresser. I assumed you'd want it. I'll book the van for Sat morning. Dev, you'll have to take the key round before then.
i wasnt going to argue 😂 i was going to say bring a flask
We're not bringing a flask
mum would have brought a flask
She would have. She'd have made us all sit down first
Sat 9am then. Bring bin bags. Not the good ones.
can someone check if the council are doing the bulky waste thing this month or is it still backed up
I'll look. It's November, I don't know who is still answering phones
The hoover's still in the cupboard under the stairs. Behind where the coats are. I checked when I went round last week
She had a list by the phone. I haven't looked at it yet
Leave the list for Sat. Don't read it on your own.
is the list about who gets the dresser 😂
Dev.
sorry
bulky waste is a fortnight wait btw so dont expect the sofa to be gone by sat
On my break. Man in bay 3 has asked me what time it is four times. Each time he thanks me like I've done something clever
I told him it's the middle of the night. He said he knows, he just likes to check
Back in the staff room. Can't sleep when I get in. Keep thinking about the list
Still in the staff room. Bay 3 has finally gone to sleep
I haven't read the list. I want that on record
Her writing on the back of the gas bill. I'd know it anywhere
Van booked for Sat 9am. Confirmation by email. Dev, key round to me or Jess by Thursday please.
Jess, do not open the list on your own
just woke up. jess why are u up at 4 that is not a good sign 😂
claire ok mum
Not a flask, Dev
Night shift. Bay 3 was asking the time. Not a sign of anything except bay 3
Off shift. Home. Blinds down, sleeping
got a lesson on rivers in 10 mins. key is in my coat. coat is on the hook. will bring it thurs
Thursday. Not the coat hook.
the hook is 200 yards from the bathroom 😂
council website says bulky waste is the 2nd of dec. so the sofa stays a fortnight. sorry jess
Sofa's not Jess's problem. It's Nana's sofa, Dev. It goes when it goes.
I wasn't going to argue about the sofa. Sat is fine
neighbours dog is in our back garden again. it has eaten a bin bag. no idea whose it is
[photo]
Is it awful that I'm glad the dresser's mine and I'm also dreading Saturday
Not awful. Saturday's the hard bit. The dresser's just a dresser x
its a very good dresser tho
Bed. Jess, you're on Thursday? Eat something first
Not on till Thurs. Sleeping till lunch like a normal person
normal person 😂 jess u work nights, you are not normal and we love u
Measured the hall. Dresser fits with about two centimetres to spare. Priya doesn't know yet
Woke up at 4 for no reason. Off shift for once and my body still thinks it's bay 3
Not opening the list. Just so everyone knows
morning. jess ur awake at 4 again 😂
thats 2 days running
Yes Dev
Has Priya been told about the dresser?
Not yet. Telling her tonight. She's going to say it won't fit
It fits. 2cm
Tell her it fits. Measure it again so she believes you
2cm is not a lot jess
It's enough Dev
council have put a sticker on our green bin saying "not collected: contaminated"
it was a pizza box. a PIZZA BOX 😂
Then put the pizza box in the right bin
it WAS the right bin. they said its contaminated
Letter came for Nana from the surgery today. Repeat prescription reminder. I opened it before I'd thought about it, then just stood there
Oh Claire. I'm sorry
Not your job to be sorry. Put it in the bin. Wasn't crying in the car park, if anyone's asking
nobody was asking 😂❤️
Dev.
sorry
neighbours dog is back in our garden. has got another bin bag. i think he's in love with the bin
[photo]
He looks very pleased with himself
Told Priya about the dresser. She said "that's not a dresser, that's a wardrobe with ambitions" and then said she'd help carry it Saturday if we need her
Tell her thanks. We'll be fine with the van and the three of us
She says she'll come anyway. She's already got the day off, she's just that sort of person
Bed. Dev, you don't need to answer that
I keep thinking about the crossword. She never once finished the last clue. Just left it and said she'd get it tomorrow
I used to do the last clue for her and she'd pretend she'd had it all along
Still awake. Going to make a cup of tea. Sit down first, obviously
